evidence_locations.excerpt: This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of three retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) variants [Lewis et al., 2021]—standard RAG, Self- RAG [Asai et al., 2024], and CoRAG [Wang et al., 2025]—across SQL query generation, REST API call generation, and a combined task requiring dynamic task classification.

This paper makes the following contributions: Comprehensive Evaluation: We present the first systematic comparison of RAG variants (standard RAG, Self-RAG, CoRAG) across SQL query generation, REST API call generation, and a combined task requiring dynamic classification, evaluated under database-only, API-only, and hybrid documentation contexts (18 experimental configurations).

We evaluated three RAG variants (standard RAG, Self-RAG, CoRAG) plus a no-RAG baseline across three task settings: (1) SQL query generation, (2) REST API call generation, and (3) a combined task where the system must first classify whether the user’s natural language request requires data retrieval (SQL) or data modification (API), then generate the appropriate code accordingly.

Following established practices in text-to-SQL [Yu et al., 2018; Pourreza and Rafiei, 2023] and API evaluation [Kim et al., 2024; Basu et al., 2025], we reported five metrics: Exact Match Accuracy, Component Match Accuracy, Execution Accuracy, Endpoint Retrieval Accuracy (API only), Classification Accuracy (combined task only).

With database-only documentation, all RAG variants achieve comparable performance: Exact match accuracy ranges from 14.45% (standard RAG) to 15.61% (Self-RAG and CoRAG), with execution accuracy near 72–73%.
Our comparative evaluation reveals that retrieval policy choice significantly impacts robustness when documentation becomes heterogeneous.
